doc.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: Building a record collection: Premier label, Conte Candoli, Herbie Mann and Sam Most
summary: He describes cheap Premier label records, Conte Candoli's first album, and the Herbie Mann album with Sam Most solos.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: All the cats, yeah, I mean that was one hell of a band. And then “Take Five,” you know the “Time Out” album. That was the other one that I got. And then we just started buying a whole bunch of things and of course we had this whole entourage of Sinatra albums. And when you’re listening to Nelson Riddle and Duke Ellington and all this stuff, I mean you’re catching the vibe of exactly what this is about. And then I just started, there used to be a label, Premier, which as I found out later exploited all of the cats that they recorded. But they had, in the eighty-nine-cent-bin in the drug stores, and things like that, you could find Premier label records and it was everybody: Conte Candoli, I had the first album, when I got to play with Conte with Doc Severinsen and the Tonight Show Band, Conte had told me that was the first album him and his brother recorded. And of course they got screwed royally on basically what happened with it but they got an album out and did what they did. And there was a whole bunch of Herbie Mann stuff. One album I bought, Herbie Mann and Sam Most.
Well an interesting little thing about that is a bunch of the solos that say they’re Herbie Mann are actually Sam Most.
Yeah. He wanted to sound better on alto.
They say it was a mistake in the liner notes, yeah it was a mistake.
